# Jubilees Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Abram Rejects Idolatry; Abram's Prayer; The Call of God; Journey to Canaan

---

**12:1** And it came to pass in the sixth week, in the seventh year thereof, that Abram said to Terah his father, saying: "Father!"

**12:2** And he said, "Behold, here am I, my son." And he said: "What help and profit have we from those idols which thou dost worship, and before which thou dost bow thyself?"

**12:3** "For there is no spirit in them, for they are dumb forms, and a misleading of the heart. Worship them not."

**12:4** "Worship the God of heaven, who causes the rain and the dew to descend on the earth and does everything upon the earth, and has created everything by his word, and all life is from before his face."

**12:5** "Why do you worship things that have no spirit in them? For they are the work of men's hands, and on your shoulders do ye bear them, and ye have no profit from them. But they are a great shame to those who make them, and a misleading of the heart to those who worship them."

**12:6** "Worship them not."

**12:7** And his father said unto him: "I also know it, my son, but what shall I do with a people who have made me to serve before them?"

**12:8** "And if I tell them the truth, they will slay me; for their soul clings to them to worship them and honor them."

**12:9** "Keep silence, my son, lest they slay thee."

**12:10** And he spoke these things to Nahor his brother; and Nahor was wroth with him and did not hearken to him, for his heart was attached to the idols.

**12:11** And Abram arose in the night, and he burned the house of the idols, and he burned all that was in the house; and no man knew it.

**12:12** And they arose in the night and sought to save their gods from the midst of the fire.

**12:13** And Haran hasted to save them, but the fire flamed over him, and he was burnt in the fire, and he died in Ur of the Chaldees before Terah his father, and they buried him.

**12:14** And Terah went forth from Ur of the Chaldees, himself and his sons, to go into the land of Lebanon and into the land of Canaan, and he dwelt in the land of Haran, and Abram dwelt with his father in Haran two weeks of years.

**12:15** And in the forty-first jubilee in the third year of the first week Abram returned to his father's house. And Terah's sons: Nahor dwelt there, and Haran was dead.

**12:16** And in the sixth year of the second week of the forty-first jubilee he sat down at night and observed the stars from the evening to the morning, in order to see what would be the character of the year with regard to the rains, and he was alone as he sat and observed.

**12:17** And a word came into his heart and he said: "All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun are all in the hand of the LORD. Why do I search them out?"

**12:18** "If he desires, he causes it to rain, morning and evening; and if he desires, he withholds it, and all things are in his hand."

**12:19** And he prayed that night and said: "My God, God Most High, thou alone art my God, and thee and thy dominion have I chosen, and thou hast created all things, and all things are the work of thy hands."

**12:20** "Deliver me from the hands of evil spirits who have dominion over the thoughts of men's hearts, and let them not lead me astray from thee, my God."

**12:21** "And establish thou me and my seed forever, that we go not astray from henceforth and for evermore."

**12:22** And he said: "Shall I return unto Ur of the Chaldees who seek my face that I may return to them, or am I to remain here in this place?"

**12:23** "The right path before thee, prosper it in the hands of thy servant that he may fulfill it and that I may not walk in the error of my heart, O my God."

**12:24** And he made an end of speaking and praying, and behold the word of the LORD was sent to him through me, saying: "Get thee up from thy country, and from thy kindred, and from the house of thy father unto a land which I will show thee, and I shall make thee a great nation, and I will bless thee and I will make thy name great, and thou wilt be blessed in the earth, and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed."

**12:25** And I will take care of all thy seed that is under the sun, as the sand of the sea-shore shall thy seed be, and I will give to thy seed a great land to inherit it for ever."

**12:26** And he arose and took Sarai his wife, and Lot, the son of Haran his brother's son, and went to the land of Canaan, and he came into the land of Asshur, and proceeded to Shechem, and dwelt near a lofty oak.

**12:27** And he saw, and behold, the land was very pleasant from the entering in of Hamath to the lofty oak.

**12:28** And the LORD said to him: "To thee and to thy seed will I give this land."

**12:29** And he built an altar there, and offered thereon a burnt offering to the LORD, who had appeared to him.

**12:30** And he removed from thence unto the mountain of Beth-el on the west and Ai on the east, and pitched his tent there.

**12:31** And he saw and behold the land was very wide and good, and everything grew thereon — vines and figs and pomegranates, oaks and ilexes, and terebinths and oil trees and cedars and cypresses and date trees and all manner of trees, and there was water on the mountains.

**12:32** And he blessed the LORD who had led him forth from Ur of the Chaldees, and had brought him safely to this land.

---
*EMET notes: Abram's astronomical observation (v.16) and subsequent rejection of astrology (v.17) = the Jubilees version of Abraham's discovery of monotheism. The divine call (v.24) is spoken through the angel of the presence ("through me") — confirming the angelic narrator throughout. Sarai (not yet renamed Sarah) and Lot accompany (v.26).*
